description_paragraphs: Assume $f=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i$, with each $f_i:\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_y}\to\mathbb{R}$ continuously differentiable. For all full-space points $z,w$,

$$
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\|\nabla f_i(z)-\nabla f_i(w)\|_2^2\le\beta^2\|z-w\|_2^2.
$$
Only the mean function $f(x,\cdot)$ must be uniformly $\mu_y$-strongly concave. Components need not be concave or individually $\beta$-smooth; $f(\cdot,y)$ and $\Phi$ may be nonconvex.

The public initial point is $(0,0)$, with promises $y^\star(0)=0$ and $\Phi(0)-\inf_x\Phi(x)\le\Delta<\infty$. Attainment of the primal minimum is not required. Assume $n\ge2$ and $\kappa=\beta/\mu_y\ge1$.

assumptions.description: For every joint variable $z,w$, $n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\|\nabla f_i(z)-\nabla f_i(w)\|^2\le\beta^2\|z-w\|^2$.

assumptions.scope: All point pairs in the declared function domain. Blockwise constants are uniform in the remaining fixed variables.
assumptions.description: For each fixed $x$, the function $-f(x,\cdot)$ is $\mu_y$-strongly convex, uniformly in $x$. This assumption applies only to the average function $f=n^{-1}\sum_i f_i$; individual components need not be strongly concave.

assumptions.scope: Public initial point; the objective-gap or distance term refers to the same solution or value function explicitly specified in this entry

assumptions.description: Neither $x\mapsto f(x,y)$ nor the optimal-value function $\Phi$ is additionally assumed convex.

$$
(i,x,y)\longmapsto\nabla f_i(x,y),\quad i\in\{1,\ldots,n\},\ (x,y)\in\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_y}.

The algorithm selects a component index and query point. Each index always refers to the same fixed component. The response is its exact full joint gradient, without a function value, Hessian, best response, or reduced gradient. There is no random oracle noise.

$$

oracle.operation: At an adaptive query (i,x,y), with i in {1,...,n} chosen by the algorithm and (x,y) anywhere in R^{d_x} x R^{d_y}, return exactly the joint gradient grad f_i(x,y).
oracle.response_exclusions: No function value, reduced gradient grad Phi, dual optimizer y*, exact maximization, Hessian, or stochastic sample-field interface is supplied.
oracle.coupling: Persistent component identities; repeated queries to a component access the same fixed function and each cost another call. Index selection is controlled by the algorithm.
oracle.conditional_law: The hidden instance is fixed before an independent private algorithm seed U. Conditional on the instance, complete past transcript, seed information used by the algorithm, and current (i_t,x_t,y_t), the response law is the point mass at grad f_{i_t}(x_t,y_t). There is no stochastic oracle error or adversarial response choice.
oracle.cost: One selected component joint-gradient call increments N_component by one. A full mean-gradient sweep costs n calls. No setup oracle calls are free.
auxiliary_interfaces: Projection uses the stated interface. Internal models defined by already returned data may be solved exactly.
